items.title: 63475_Arnett Cobb oral history interview
items.q: But when Tiny Bradshaw came in, his contract didn't mean nothing.

ctx.x: Well, what were we gonna do? But we went in and got six Chicago musicians and that put us in. Politics. and Now, we didn't know that. But when Tiny Bradshaw came in, his contract didn't mean nothing. Took it down to Harry Grave's office, who was the President of the union, and it didn't mean nothing and just tear it up. That's what he told Charlie Graham, who was running the Rum Boogie.
Milton Larkin's band stayed at the Rum Boogie 9 months. I stayed five of the nine and joined him.
